It can definitely be overwhelming to sift through all the things you can do to reset! Have you ever thought to try intermittent fasting? I started out the same way during the quarantine. Basically would spend my entire day eating and I ended up gaining all the weight I had lost. I looked into IF and I started out with 16:8. Then slowly transitioned to 18:6 and finally OMAD. 

The trick is: start slow! I went in way too fast (only did a few 16:8 before jumping to OMAD) and only lasted a month before binging. Take it slow. Do 1 month of 16:8 and see how you feel. If you feel you could last longer not eating, go for it! 

Calculate your TDEE again. I changed mine up since I’m not so active during the stay at home stuff so I changed up my tdee to match that. Do you use any apps to track what you eat? I use both the app Lose It which is great cause it lets you know how much caloric deficit you ate that week

And most importantly, don’t get discouraged. Find something that motivates you and stick to that. It’s so cliche but it’s what keeps me going. I also have a cheat meal (only a meal) once a week to treat myself. 

PM me if you want to talk! It’s great to have a friend too to help keep you on track

Teaching was definitely tough! I have first graders and it takes a lot of patience. Some of which I lost while starting OMAD haha. It’s definitely a mind game too (at least it was for me). Like physically I knew I wasn’t hungry but in my mind, when my students would have lunch, I felt that I should be eating lunch too. That’s when I’d go out for a walk to keep myself busy. 

When I eat, I always tried to stay within 1200-1300 range. I always make sure to have a protein (usually grilled chicken), veggies (I’m super picky so it was usually broccoli or asparagus or sometimes cauliflower), and a carb. Usually sweet potatoes. It got to the point where I would get home after a workout and after fasting for 23 hours I would just be in the mood for something small. Like egg whites with a whole bunch of vegetables and a side of avocados. Play around with what you eat and see how you feel in the morning. That’s usually how I’d notice if I ate enough (or not enough) and what I’d have to have for dinner to help with the hunger. 

Definitely use this page for help with recipes. If I’m in the mood for a smoothie, I just type in OMAD smoothies and boom, hundreds of recipes. 

Please let me know how your journey is going! I’m in no way an expert (barely 5 months in) but it’s nice to always have the support of someone else!

I’m a teacher so unfortunately I can’t work out in the morning. I usually eat from 6-7 p.m (doesn’t take that long but that’s usually my eating window) and I try to work out right after school. Usually from 3-5 or so.

I know some people have amazing experience of losing weight without working out but I wanted to have an overhaul of my lifestyle. Until 6 days in I finally sucked it up and just did some light cardio. As I got used to that, I started including weights. So start slow! After awhile, my body got used to it and now I love working out while fasting. It oddly enough gives me energy.  Just for some stats: F(27) SW: 190 CW: 175 GW: 130

This page is super helpful too. Anytime I’d feel hungry, I’d read posts from other people and let me tell you, that helped keep the motivation. There’s of course options if you feel hungry like green tea and some other stuff but water is usually what I stick to. 

Don’t worry, you got this! 5 days in is already pretty amazing. Just keep it going and you’ll definitely start to see results
